newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania defends Congo's Kabila over elections.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania defends Congo's Kabila over elections.

text.p: Tanzanian president Benjamin Mkapa defended Congo's new ruler Laurent Kabila on Wednesday over the timing of elections and said calls for an early poll were absurd.

"To ask Kabila to call for elections even before he has...created necessary institutions and capacities to do so is not only an expression of arrogance and ignorance, but completely absurd," Mkapa told a meeting of African Commonwealth countries.

African states including South Africa and Uganda have defended a statement by the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) that it would take up to two years to prepare for elections.

Kabila declared himself president and changed the country's name to the Democratic Republic of Congo on May 17 after AFDL troops entered the capital Kinshasa ousting former president Mobutu Sese Seko who relinquished power.
Since then Kabila has been under pressure from the U.S. and France to form a broad-based government and hold early elections.
